label: Saved example, written for this demo
note: Key facts for eight demo disputes, so the feature shows without an API key. Each fact carries a word-for-word quote from its document, and a test checks that every quote is really in the document.

facts.fact: The signed scope promised 12 mobile app screens in Figma with 2 revision rounds.
facts.quote: 12 mobile app screens in Figma, 2 revision rounds

facts.fact: The customer signed it on 30 May 2026.
On 20 Jun 2026 the customer approved milestone 2 and all 12 screens in writing.
facts.quote: Approved milestone 2. All 12 screens look great

facts.fact: The customer told the merchant to go ahead with the final handoff.
The customer opened the design file on 22 Jun, 25 Jun and 14 Jul 2026.
facts.quote: viewed 'Brightline App v3' on 22 Jun, 25 Jun and 14 Jul 2026

facts.fact: The customer made their own copy of the file on 14 Jul 2026.
The terms say the plan renews every year and must be cancelled in Settings > Billing before the renewal date.
facts.quote: Renews annually; cancel in Settings > Billing before the renewal date

facts.fact: The customer accepted these terms on 3 Aug 2025.
On 29 Jul 2026 the customer said they were thinking of cancelling. That is not a cancellation.
facts.quote: Honestly I'm thinking of cancelling, not using it much.

facts.fact: The support agent pointed them to Settings > Billing. There were no more messages.
facts.quote: You can cancel from Settings > Billing any time.

facts.fact: The customer's last login was 28 Jul 2026, with none after.
The billing audit log shows no cancellation action.
The booker accepted a 50% refund for cancellations 7 to 14 days before departure.
facts.quote: 7 to 14 days before departure get a 50% refund

facts.fact: The cancellation came from a different email address than the one that booked.
The merchant said it only accepts cancellations from the booker, and nothing followed.
facts.quote: We can only accept cancellations from the booker.

facts.fact: The customer ticked 'I agree' to the terms on 1 May 2024, and the terms say no refunds after renewal.
The terms say the plan renews every year and can be cancelled before the renewal date.
facts.quote: Renews annually. Cancel any time before the renewal date.

facts.fact: A renewal reminder went to the customer on 17 Apr 2026, two weeks before renewal.
facts.quote: Renewal reminder sent to tom@northfieldco.com on 17 Apr 2026

facts.fact: The customer asked to cancel on 4 May 2026, which is after the renewal date.
The customer logged in on four dates in May 2026 after cancelling and ran report exports.
The sales page promised 8 weekly live mentoring sessions.
The merchant's own record says no live sessions were held.
The student asked for a refund on 10 Jun 2026 and got no reply.
facts.quote: I paid for live sessions and none happened. Please refund.

facts.fact: The guest ticked an acceptance of the 7-day non-refundable rule on 1 Apr 2026.
facts.quote: cancellations within 7 days of departure are non-refundable

facts.fact: The guest cancelled on 17 May 2026, 3 days before departure.
The merchant pointed to the accepted policy and offered a free move to a later date.
facts.quote: We can move you to a later date at no cost.

facts.fact: The 7-day rule is only on a Terms page linked from the site footer.
The booking email does not mention the policy and checkout had no acceptance box.
The merchant refused the refund by pointing to its terms.
facts.quote: our terms say no refunds within 7 days
